chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated, saying: Hamza ibn al-Qasim al-Alawi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from one who entered upon Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi (peace be upon him) from the people of Rayy, saying:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Where were you?' I said: 'I visited al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Indeed, if you had visited the grave of Abdul Azim (peace be upon him) with you, it would be as if you had visited al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الرَّیِّ: The people of Rayy, a city near modern-day Tehran
key_terms.الزِّيَارَة: Ziyarat, the act of visiting a shrine or grave for spiritual benefit
key_terms.الْعَسْکَرِیِّ: Al-Askari, a title referring to the district of Samarra where the Imams resided
key_terms.عَبْدُ الْعَظِيمِ: Abdul Azim al-Hasani, a prominent companion of the Imams buried in Rayy

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Abdul Azim in Rayy according to Imam al-Hadi?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the unique spiritual merit of the shrine of Abdul Azim al-Hasani in Rayy, equating its reward to that of Imam Husayn (a.s.) himself. This comparison underscores the high status of the Imams' descendants and companions in Shia tradition, where visiting their graves is considered a means of drawing closer to the Ahl al-Bayt. The specific mention of Rayy reflects the historical importance of this region as a center of Shia scholarship and pilgrimage during the era of the Twelve Imams.
